current.text: Dejounte Murray starts at point guard ahead of Fears, which limits his lead guard role.

Fears and Herb Jones compete for the last starting spot next to Murray, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson and likely Yves Missi. Joe Dumars is reported to want Fears to start, and a Pelicans beat reporter expects him to start over Jones.
He is the most likely player to replace Herb Jones in the starting lineup. Josh gives him at least a 50/50 chance to start.
The Pelicans roster is crowded with high-usage players. Experts see no clear 30-minute role for Fears, and minutes are hard to project.
If Dejounte Murray is traded or hurt, Fears could give top 70 numbers.
He shot 33% from three last season.
His big games late last season came with steals and volume that one expert calls fake, so a repeat of that level is doubtful.
He looked good in his most recent game.

Experts treat him as a late upside flyer, taken between round 9 and round 12 (around picks 104 to 135). One expert calls him badly under drafted if he lasts to round 13. Josh moved him up but takes him only if he starts.
New Orleans plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (season ending March 28).
New Orleans has a league-high 16 back-to-backs.
New head coach Jamahl Mosley brings a defense-first identity.
The Pelicans are projected as a weak team near the bottom of the West, at about 34 wins.

durable.text: He is a downhill lead guard who is dynamic with the ball and keeps attacking the rim even when he is not scoring there.
He is not a good enough three-point shooter to play off the ball as a two guard, and he is slightly undersized.
He is not a good defender.

note: Fears is a bubble player for our 144-player draft. Yahoo and ESPN price him at about 1 to 2 USD, and he went undrafted in our league last season. Experts like him as a late upside flyer, mostly for steals and assists. His projected FG% (43.8%) and turnovers (2.3) are a drag, so he fits best as a 1 USD final pick, especially on a team that also drafted Dejounte Murray as his handcuff. In the first weeks, check whether he starts over Herb Jones and gets close to 30 minutes. If he comes off the bench in a crowded rotation, he is an easy drop, and the 4-4-3 playoff schedule only matters if he holds a real role.
